title: City of Golden Shadow
author: Williams, Tad
review:
This is really like ten books in one, every chapter changes it up and is often in a completely different genre. One of the most ambitious book ones I've read, there's a huge amount of disparate storylines that are distinct and hugely different and it's not clear how they'll all converge, but they're all enjoyable and crafted with care.

Has some pacing issues like pretty much every Tad Williams book I've read which is the biggest issue, but doesn't impact the novel that significantly. The writing is beautiful. Tad Williams is one of my favorite authors for setting a scene and immersing you in a moment, even though the world is strange and often horrifying there's moments of serenity and beauty that take your breath away with how they're described.

highlights.text: He was sitting on a beach, an inarguable beach, staring at his own dream. And before that, he had passed through a nightmare.
